newsitem.title: USA: Germany, France pressed to cut rates at OECD meet.
newsitem.headline: Germany, France pressed to cut rates at OECD meet.

text.p: Germany and France came under pressure to cut interest rates at a meeting of economic policymakers from industrial countries last week, international monetary sources said on Monday.
But the two countries resisted, arguing that their economies were improving and were not in need of stimulus at this time, the sources, who declined to be identified, said.
Much of the pressure, which came at a meeting of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development's Working Party Three group, seemed to emanate from the International Monetary Fund.
The United States, which in the past has often led the way in calling for lower interest rates in Europe, refrained from doing so this time, the sources said.

Some sources argued that rate cuts would help boost corporate and consumer confidence as the two countries struggle to meet the tough budget criteria required for participation in European monetary union.
But others questioned the usefulness of such action now, given the lag in time before changes in monetary policy affect an economy, and said Europe needed to focus more on structural reform.
